pit_signals_detected: B2C subscription model in Peru fails because 70-75% of workforce is informal and 36% live below $8.30/day — students and parents have negligible WTP for a paid study app; any pricing above free is a barrier.

Free substitutes already dominate: students use WhatsApp groups, YouTube tutorials, Khan Academy, and MINEDU's free digital resources (e.g., Aprendo en Casa). A gamified wrapper is not enough to switch from these ubiquitous zero-cost options.

Behavior change is notoriously hard: students lack intrinsic motivation for a standalone study app; gamification has short novelty; retention decays quickly without institutional enforcement (teachers assigning it). Without embedding into school workflow, daily active use is unlikely.

Market size illusion: even if 10M students in Peru, only ~2-3M have consistent internet access and ability to pay. Realistic paying users in first 12 months likely <5,000 — not venture scale without regional expansion.

MINEDU could launch a free gamified study platform (e.g., as part of PeruEduca) or partner with existing edtech nonprofits — a government-funded free alternative would collapse the value proposition overnight.
classification_rationale: Gamified study companion addresses student motivation, a recurring but non-urgent problem. In Peru, B2C edtech faces low willingness to pay and high competition from free resources. No structural pain or regulatory forcing function.
freemium_rationale: Freemium model aligns with low WTP in Peru; free tier builds user base while premium features (e.g., advanced analytics, unlimited sessions) monetize a small percentage of dedicated users.
payment_blocker: Students/parents have near-zero willingness to pay for a study companion; the vast majority cannot afford any subscription (S/10-20/month is already prohibitive for 70% of population), and those who can already use free tools or pay for tutoring.
free_substitute_risk: WhatsApp study groups, YouTube explainer videos, free resources from MINEDU (Aprendo en Casa, PeruEduca), and free apps like Duolingo or Kahoot! cover 90% of the 'gamified study' use case at zero cost.
market_size_reality_check: Realistic SOM in Peru: ~200,000 students with strong WTP (upper-middle-class in Lima), but conversion to paid subscription <2% → 4,000 users at S/20/month = S/80,000/month (~$21K) — not enough for a VC-backed startup; regional expansion needed but adds complexity cost.
hardest_assumption: That students will consistently use and pay for a standalone gamified study app without integration into school curriculum or teacher mandate — a pattern that has failed globally (most edtech B2C apps have <30% retention after 1 month).
devil_rationale: StudyPet faces a triple threat: no effective monetization in Peru's low-WTP, informal economy; abundant free substitutes that students already use; and extreme difficulty in changing student behavior without school buy-in. The idea is a nice-to-have, not a must-have, and can't reach venture scale without a radical pivot (e.g., B2B selling to schools or embedding in government curriculum).
